thread:
meera: Hey team — I need to remove my mom (dependent) from my medical & dental plans. Guardianship ended 2025-03-15 per court order. What docs do you need and when would coverage stop? I'm worried about payroll deductions and COBRA options.
people-ops: Sorry to hear about the change, Meera. We can start this for you. We need a copy of the court order or official documentation showing termination of guardianship, plus a completed QLE form. Can you upload both to the benefits portal? :folded_hands:
meera: Uploaded the court order PDF to the portal just now (under "attachments") and filled the QLE form. Let me know if anything else is missing.
people-ops: Got them — I see the upload. Thanks! Quick note on effective date: the carrier typically accepts the QLE effective date as the event date (2025-03-15), but some carriers enforce end-of-month rules. We'll submit 3/15 as the requested effective date and confirm carrier response. If carrier requires end-of-month, we'll adjust and notify you.
kelvin: Payroll heads-up — our payroll cutoff for April's premiums is 2025-03-20. If benefits change is submitted and approved before the cutoff, we can prorate premiums for the rest of March/April depending on payroll cycles. If it's after cutoff, the deduction change will appear on next cycle and we may need to do a retro adj.
meera: Thanks @kelvin. If the carrier accepts 3/15 as the effective date, how will the proration work? Example premiums would help.
payroll: Example: assume monthly dependent premium = $160. If coverage ends 2025-03-15, that's 17 days coverage in March (1–15 inclusive) out of 31. Proration formula we use is pro-rated charge = monthly_premium * (days_covered / days_in_month). So: ```160 * (15/31) = $77.42 charged for March dependent portion``` then the remainder would not be charged. If we already deducted full month earlier, we'll issue a refund/credit on next paycheck or apply to next month depending on timing.
meera: Super clear, thanks. Do I need to opt into COBRA for my mom or is she eligible?
people-ops: Typically, COBRA is offered only when the covered person's eligibility ends and the covered person is the employee or their spouse/dependent — eligibility varies by plan and by dependent category. Since this is a dependent losing eligibility due to guardianship ending, carriers usually offer COBRA for the dependent. We'll confirm and send the COBRA notice after carrier confirms the termination. You don't need to elect it immediately; COBRA notice gives a 60-day election window.
meera: Good to know. If COBRA is offered, will I still be able to keep her on the payroll deduction line until she elects?
payroll: We stop employer coverage as of the effective date. If COBRA is elected, COBRA premiums are billed separately (carrier or administrator) — not via our regular payroll deductions. So payroll won't continue to deduct for the dependent after the termination effective date.
people-ops: Next steps for us: 1) submit the QLE + court order to the carrier today 2) confirm effective date with carrier (we'll update this thread) 3) if carrier requires end-of-month, we'll request an exception if possible and otherwise schedule termination for 3/31 4) send COBRA notice if applicable.
meera: Appreciate it. One last question — does this affect my FSA dependent care or HSA? My dependent care FSA currently has recurring claims.
elizabeth: tagging in HR benefits specialist — dependent care FSA is affected if you were using dependent care for that person. If the dependent is no longer eligible for dependent care, you can't submit new claims for them after the QLE effective date. Existing claims already incurred prior to termination are still valid. For HSA there's no dependent-specific enrollment; HSA eligibility is tied to your plan tier.
people-ops: @meera, I'll follow up with the COBRA timeline and carrier response here within 48 hours.
people-ops-bot: Ticket #B-3472 created for "Dependent removal / QLE - Meera" and assigned to benefits team. ETA carrier response ~2 business days. :spiral_calendar:
meera: Thanks everyone — leaving this open here for updates. :pray:
